newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian PM calls for courageous GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian PM calls for courageous GDP growth.

text.p: Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday Australia should have the courage to greatly accelerate its economic growth rate.
The Reserve Bank manipulates domestic demand with overnight cash rates, which the central bank has progressively cut to 5.0 percent from 7.5 percent in five equal reductions over the past year.
Howard's comment backs Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane, who said in a speech on Tuesday Australia's economy could grow faster than currently projected without sparking an inflation surge.
"It's a declaration that we ought to have the courage and we ought to have the capacity to grow at a much faster rate," Howard said in a speech to members of the ruling Liberal Party.
"We have to grow the economy at a faster rate -- at least four percent per year or more."
Macfarlane, reflecting on the subdued outlook for inflation, said Australia could aim for 4.5 percent economic growth or more over the next few years.

The economy slowed last year and gross domestic product grew just 2.4 percent between the March quarters of 1996 and 1997. Its long-run trend growth is about 3.2 percent, which economists say is not enough to dent unemployment.
The unemployment rate has been stagnant at about 8.5 percent for the past two years.
The government has forecast economic growth of 3.75 percent in fiscal 1997/98, from July 1.
